given: a 3.3 volt rail reaching an unloaded input through a 4.7 kilohm pull-up
then: an analog sense on the input reads the solved voltage, the rail's full 3.3 volts

given: a 3.3 volt rail reaching an unloaded input through a 4.7 kilohm pull-up
then: a digital sense on the same input reads it as pulled high through the 4.7 kilohms
why: a digital reader wants the pull-up view, which a numeric solve would replace with a bare voltage

given: several agreeing drivers on separate nets, chained by resistors into one cluster that carries an analog sense
then: with 2 drivers, the cluster is solved once, its sources handed over in the order their pins were registered
why: the order the solver receives sources is the order their contributions are summed, and a summation order that varies between passes moves the last bits of the solved voltage

given: several agreeing drivers on separate nets, chained by resistors into one cluster that carries an analog sense
then: with 3 drivers, the cluster is solved once, its sources handed over in the order their pins were registered
why: the order the solver receives sources is the order their contributions are summed, and a summation order that varies between passes moves the last bits of the solved voltage

given: several agreeing drivers on separate nets, chained by resistors into one cluster that carries an analog sense
then: with 8 drivers, the cluster is solved once, its sources handed over in the order their pins were registered
why: the order the solver receives sources is the order their contributions are summed, and a summation order that varies between passes moves the last bits of the solved voltage

given: a push-pull pin driving one net, joined by a series resistor to a net carrying a 3.3 volt rail
then: a high driver agreeing with the rail keeps its digital level however close the rail is, and nothing is solved

given: a push-pull pin driving one net, joined by a series resistor to a net carrying a 3.3 volt rail
then: a low driver with the rail within ten times its own impedance sends both nets through the analog solver, which sets their states

given: a push-pull pin driving one net, joined by a series resistor to a net carrying a 3.3 volt rail
then: a low driver with the rail beyond that ratio keeps its digital level, the rail's net keeps its voltage, and nothing is solved

given: a pin driving high and a pin driving low on separate nets joined by a series resistor
then: through 47 ohms, both nets are in contention
why: for signalling purposes two nets joined by a small series resistance are one node, so drivers disagreeing across it are fighting

given: a pin driving high and a pin driving low on separate nets joined by a series resistor
then: the contention finding names both fighting pins

given: a pin driving high and a pin driving low on separate nets joined by a series resistor
then: through exactly 1 kilohm, the collapse limit itself, neither net is in contention

given: two equal 4.7 kilohm resistors in series between a 3.3 volt rail and ground, with no push-pull driver anywhere
then: the midpoint reads the divided voltage, 1.65 volts

given: two equal 4.7 kilohm resistors in series between a 3.3 volt rail and ground, with no push-pull driver anywhere
then: nothing is reported for it

given: a reserved place in the drive order that is never filled, with the next drive arriving normally behind it
then: the skip is reported as a finding naming the missing place in the order

given: a reserved place in the drive order that is never filled, with the next drive arriving normally behind it
then: after a bounded wait the gap is skipped and the waiting drive takes effect

given: a reserved place in the drive order that is never filled, with the next drive arriving normally behind it
then: for a short while the later drive waits, in case the missing one is merely late

given: a pin driving one net, and a second net reached from it only through a 47 ohm series resistor
then: driven high, the far net reads high as well, pulled through the resistor's 47 ohms
why: a driven signal keeps its level across a series resistor, so a receiver behind one sees every bit its driver sends

given: a pin driving one net, and a second net reached from it only through a 47 ohm series resistor
then: driven low, the far net reads low as well, pulled through the resistor's 47 ohms
why: a driven signal keeps its level across a series resistor, so a receiver behind one sees every bit its driver sends

given: two pins on one net whose drives reach the engine in the opposite order to the one they were issued in
then: the fight between the two pins is reported as a contention finding while the engine runs

given: two pins on one net whose drives reach the engine in the opposite order to the one they were issued in
then: observers see the net driven by the first drive and then in contention once the second lands
why: the order drives were issued is the authoritative event order, whatever order they cross the queue in

given: two pins on one net whose drives reach the engine in the opposite order to the one they were issued in
then: the drive issued second takes no effect while the one issued first is still on its way

given: two step-clock sources on one line, 47 ohms apart, with a drive input beyond them
then: neither source gets a route

given: two step-clock sources on one line, 47 ohms apart, with a drive input beyond them
then: exactly one finding is raised, naming both sources as a mismatched pair
why: two step clocks driving one line is the same wiring error as two transmitters on one serial line

given: a random board of up to nine nets with shorts, resistors, drivers at assorted impedances, rails, injected faults and senses, under a random sequence of drive changes
then: after every change, the accumulated findings equal those of the full pass

given: a random board of up to nine nets with shorts, resistors, drivers at assorted impedances, rails, injected faults and senses, under a random sequence of drive changes
then: after the first pass and after every change, each net's state equals what a full pass over the whole board gives
why: clusters are electrically independent, so re-resolving only the cluster a drive touched is exact

given: a pin handle and a component's timing interface that are attached to no engine
then: driving the pin and requesting wakeups do nothing and raise no error

given: a pin handle and a component's timing interface that are attached to no engine
then: the pin reads as floating

given: a low-driving pin behind 10 kilohms, a middle net, and 47 ohms beyond it a far net where a short to 3.3 volts can be injected
then: with nothing injected, the middle net is pulled low by the driver

given: a low-driving pin behind 10 kilohms, a middle net, and 47 ohms beyond it a far net where a short to 3.3 volts can be injected
then: with the short injected, the middle net is pulled high; the zero-ohm fault outvotes the driver behind ten kilohms
why: an injected short is an ideal source and ranks like a declared rail, so a fault someone injected is visible from every net it reaches

given: two components requesting wakeups at instants already in the past, the later instant requested first
then: both fire, the earlier deadline first, whichever was requested first

given: a single wakeup requested 100 virtual milliseconds ahead
then: the wake is delivered stamped at or after the requested instant

given: a single wakeup requested 100 virtual milliseconds ahead
then: it is delivered exactly once

given: a wakeup requested every 20 virtual milliseconds
then: the component keeps being woken, period after period

given: a wakeup requested every 20 virtual milliseconds
then: the delivered timestamps never go backwards

given: a one-shot wakeup requested for exactly the instant a component's periodic wakeup is first due, with time held while both are armed
then: the component is woken once at the shared instant and again at each following period

given: a step-clock source reaching one drive input through two 47 ohm resistors and another input through a 4.7 kilohm isolation resistor
then: one route is derived, carrying the source to the input behind the small resistors alone
why: series resistance below 1 kilohm is part of the link, and an isolation resistor marks where a step clock stops

given: a step-clock source reaching one drive input through two 47 ohm resistors and another input through a 4.7 kilohm isolation resistor
then: nothing is reported

given: a step-clock source with nothing connected to it, and a drive input on another net with nothing connected either
then: nothing is reported for either

given: a step-clock source with nothing connected to it, and a drive input on another net with nothing connected either
then: the source keeps a route with no inputs on it
why: a source's current train is retained on its route, so an input attached later can be served straight away

given: two threads each driving its own pin on one shared net at the same moment
then: each drive is applied on its own: the net is seen driven by whichever landed first before it is seen contended

given: two threads each driving its own pin on one shared net at the same moment
then: once both have landed the net is in contention

given: one component requesting the same wakeup instant fifty times and a later instant once, all before time is released
then: the component is woken once at the first instant and once at the second
why: one wake per component per instant, so a handler that re-arms itself from every wake stays at one wake per edge

given: six drivers at assorted voltages and impedances tied into one node by zero-ohm links, with a ground rail 37 ohms away, resolved from scratch sixty-four times
then: every pass solves the node to the same voltage, bit for bit
why: resolution is a pure function of the drive table, so a run can be replayed and compared bit for bit

given: six drivers at assorted voltages and impedances tied into one node by zero-ohm links, with a ground rail 37 ohms away, resolved from scratch sixty-four times
then: every pass hands the solver the same list: the drivers in pin order, then the rail

given: a sense handler that crashes on every delivery, beside a well-behaved sense on the same net, as the net is driven
then: the crash is reported as a finding naming the net

given: a sense handler that crashes on every delivery, beside a well-behaved sense on the same net, as the net is driven
then: the engine stays alive
why: net service for every other component survives one component's misbehaviour

given: a sense handler that crashes on every delivery, beside a well-behaved sense on the same net, as the net is driven
then: the well-behaved sense keeps receiving deliveries

given: two nets whose senses each drive the other's pin high on seeing a high, closing a feedback loop
then: the loop settles: each net is seen to change exactly once and then nothing more is delivered

given: two nets whose senses each drive the other's pin high on seeing a high, closing a feedback loop
then: a drive issued from inside a sense takes effect in a later pass, after that sense has returned
why: senses are delivered with no engine lock held, so a loop through driver, net and sense is deadlock-free by construction

given: an engine parked on a wakeup a virtual minute away when its handle is dropped
then: the engine shuts down and is joined promptly, the pending wakeup abandoned

given: a 3.3 volt rail with a short injected onto the same net
then: a short to the rail's own voltage leaves the net at that voltage with nothing reported

given: a 3.3 volt rail with a short injected onto the same net
then: a short to ground puts the net in contention
why: two ideal sources that disagree are a fight the operator must see, whichever was declared first

given: a 3.3 volt rail with a short injected onto the same net
then: the fight is reported as a contention finding

given: a component re-arming itself one bit period ahead from inside its own wake handler, while another thread floods the engine with drives
then: every wake lands exactly one bit period after the one before it
why: virtual time waits for every requested wakeup to be armed before it advances, so a bit clock is never delivered late and a byte's edges keep their spacing

given: a component re-arming itself one bit period ahead from inside its own wake handler, while another thread floods the engine with drives
then: the bit clock keeps ticking under the flood, twenty wakes delivered

given: a sense on a rail whose voltage is not modelled, which drives a pin every time it is delivered
then: the rail reads as pulled high with no series resistance

given: a sense on a rail whose voltage is not modelled, which drives a pin every time it is delivered
then: the sense fires exactly once, at registration, and the pass its own drive causes leaves it silent

given: a sense on a rail whose voltage is not modelled, which drives a pin every time it is delivered
then: the drive made from the registration delivery takes effect on its pin

given: a sense on a power rail whose voltage is not modelled, while an unrelated net is driven back and forth ten times
then: the rail's sense is delivered once, at registration, reading pulled high, and none of the ten passes deliver it again
why: a rail with an unmodelled voltage must still project a definite level that compares equal to itself across passes, so its senses fire only on a real change

given: eight wakeups requested 500 nanoseconds apart, one bit period at 2 megabaud
then: all eight fire, each stamped with exactly its own requested instant
why: at 2 megabaud eight bit edges fit inside one microsecond, and a timebase that cannot tell them apart collapses a synthesised waveform to one edge

given: a wakeup requested 10 virtual milliseconds ahead while another thread floods the engine with drives without pause
then: the wakeup is still delivered while the flood is sustained
why: drives are applied in bounded batches, so time can always advance to the next deadline however busy the drivers are

given: a stream of bytes with no idle gap between them, and the receiver is read only once the last has ended
then: every byte comes out, in the order sent
why: the edge that opens a frame closes the one before it, so decoding cannot depend on how often the receiver is read

given: a link configured 8N1 at a stated baud rate
then: one bit lasts one second divided by the baud rate

given: a link configured 8N1 at a stated baud rate
then: a frame lasts ten bit periods

given: a link configured 8N1 at a stated baud rate
then: a frame is ten bits: one start, eight data, one stop

given: each of the 256 byte values, sent alone on an otherwise idle line
then: the receiver reads back the value that was sent

given: a sender a fraction fast streams bytes back to back, with no idle gap, into a receiver at the nominal rate
then: every byte of the burst decodes, in the order sent
why: a sender's clock is never exactly nominal; a real receiver accepts the next start bit from the midpoint of the stop bit, which grants half a bit of tolerance either way

given: an all-ones byte arriving on an idle line, its only edge the start bit
then: read at that instant, the byte comes out and no completion time remains

given: an all-ones byte arriving on an idle line, its only edge the start bit
then: before the start bit, the receiver names no completion time

given: an all-ones byte arriving on an idle line, its only edge the start bit
then: once the start bit falls, the receiver names the frame's completion time as one full frame after it
why: a listener that only hears about edges has to arm a timer for this, since a frame whose tail is silent has no edge to close it

given: an all-ones byte arriving on an idle line, its only edge the start bit
then: edges inside the frame leave that time unchanged

given: a start bit has fallen and the receiver is asked for a byte a moment before the frame's nominal end
then: no byte is reported
why: the half-bit tolerance is for a frame the next start bit closes; a frame the clock closes runs its full nominal length

given: a hand-written waveform for a known byte, least-significant bit first, that is played onto the line bit by bit
then: the receiver reads the byte the waveform encodes
why: sender and receiver would agree with each other even with the bit order reversed, so the order is checked against a reference neither of them produced

given: the line falls and stays low past where the stop bit should be
then: the frame is reported as a framing error

given: the line falls and stays low past where the stop bit should be
then: a byte sent after the line returns to idle decodes cleanly
why: a break must not poison every frame that follows it

given: a link configured most-significant bit first, carrying a byte whose bit pattern is not symmetric
then: the receiver reads back the byte that was sent

given: a link configured most-significant bit first, carrying a byte whose bit pattern is not symmetric
then: the levels put on the line differ from those the same byte produces least-significant bit first

given: a sender a fraction slow streams bytes back to back, with no idle gap, into a receiver at the nominal rate
then: every byte of the burst decodes, in the order sent
why: the receiver's half-bit tolerance holds in both directions

given: a byte with no transition among its data bits: all zeros, or all ones
then: the all-ones byte decodes as all ones
why: its data, stop bit and the idle after are one unbroken high run, so no edge ever marks the frame's end; the receiver closes it on the clock

given: a byte with no transition among its data bits: all zeros, or all ones
then: the all-zeros byte decodes as zero
why: its start bit and eight data bits are one unbroken low run; the receiver only hears about level changes, so bit counts come from how long a level is held
